summary: Ittoqqortoormiit Heliport (OBY) serves one of the most remote inhabited settlements on Earth, located on the east coast of Greenland within the vast Scoresby Sund fjord system. Established to provide year-round access to a community of roughly 400 people, the heliport is a vital lifeline in a region where sea ice blocks ship access for much of the year. The settlement itself was founded in 1925 by Danish explorer Ejnar Mikkelsen and remains a gateway for expeditions into some of the world's most pristine Arctic wilderness.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Ittoqqortoormiit Heliport?
A: Air Greenland provides scheduled helicopter service connecting the settlement with other Greenlandic communities and regional hubs.

Q: Can I fly here from outside Greenland directly?
A: No, travelers must first arrive in Greenland, typically via Kangerlussuaq or Nerlerit Inaat/Constable Pynt, and then connect onward by helicopter.

Q: Why is helicopter the main transport option?
A: The settlement's extreme remoteness and surrounding sea ice for much of the year make fixed-wing operations impractical; helicopters are the most reliable link to the outside world.

Q: Is Ittoqqortoormiit open to tourists?
A: Yes, it is a popular base for Arctic expeditions focused on polar wildlife and the Scoresby Sund fjord system, though travel requires planning around weather and limited flights.
transport_tips: All arrivals and departures use helicopter, and schedules are heavily dependent on weather—build flexibility into your itinerary.
